metadata.name: Experimental Scientific Systems (ESS) Framework
metadata.purpose: Model experimental systems for scientific discovery and inverse problem solving
metadata.domain: Experimental physics, chemistry, materials science (beamlines, laboratories, field experiments)
metadata.created_for: Beamline experimentation at synchrotron facilities (NSLS2, ALS, APS, etc.)
metadata.key_innovation: Supports 'knowledge gap' nodes for inverse problem solving via matrix-based gap closure (SVD)

framework_philosophy.core_principle: Model the KNOWN experimental components (sources, manipulators, environments, detectors) to mathematically infer the UNKNOWN (sample properties, hidden mechanisms)
framework_philosophy.inverse_problem_approach: Define System D (knowledge gap) as a node with unknown properties, then use DAG → Matrix transformation → SVD gap closure to infer System D characteristics
scientific_discovery_workflow: 1. Model experimental apparatus as system-of-systems graph
2. Identify 'knowledge gap' nodes (unknown sample properties, hidden mechanisms)
4. Apply SVD-based gap closure (tools/reflow_gap_closure.py) to infer unknown properties

system_categories.description: High-level categorization of experimental components into functional systems

system_a_source.name: System A - Energy/Particle Source
system_a_source.description: Primary source of energy, particles, or excitation (X-rays, electrons, photons, etc.)

system_b_manipulation.name: System B - Mechanical/Optical Manipulation
system_b_manipulation.description: Components that manipulate, focus, steer, or condition the source

system_c_environment.name: System C - Environmental Conditions
system_c_environment.description: Controlled environmental parameters surrounding the sample

system_d_sample.name: System D - Sample Properties (KNOWLEDGE GAP)
system_d_sample.description: The sample under investigation - the primary unknown in the experiment
system_d_sample.gap_closure_approach: Infer from Systems A, B, C, E using matrix-based gap detection and SVD

system_e_detection.name: System E - Detection/Measurement
system_e_detection.description: Components that detect, measure, and record experimental observables

KNOWN.description: Component with well-characterized properties (measured, engineered, or controlled)
KNOWN.modeling_approach: Define properties explicitly in architecture file

UNKNOWN.description: Component with properties to be discovered (the scientific target)
UNKNOWN.modeling_approach: Define as 'knowledge gap' node with placeholder properties, infer via gap closure

PARTIALLY_KNOWN.description: Component with some known properties and some unknowns (constrained problem)
PARTIALLY_KNOWN.modeling_approach: Define known constraints, infer remaining properties via gap closure
examples: Known crystal symmetry, unknown lattice parameters

source_to_manipulation.description: Energy/particle transmission from source through optical/mechanical system

manipulation_to_sample.observability: MEDIUM (incident beam measurable, interaction partially observable)

environment_to_sample.observability: MEDIUM (environmental parameters measured, sample response inferred)

sample_to_detection.observability: HIGH (directly measured - this is the experimental DATA)
sample_to_detection.critical_for_gap_closure: This interaction encodes sample properties (System D) in measurement (System E)

manipulation_to_detection.description: Direct paths bypassing sample (e.g., reference measurements, alignment beams)

best_for: Synchrotron beamline experiments (X-ray scattering, spectroscopy, imaging)
visualization_types: Experimental system-of-systems graph (Source → Manipulation → Sample → Detection)

deployment_characteristics.rationale: Experimental systems are physical apparatus, not IT services

dag.reason: CRITICAL - Experimental systems are inherently causal (source → manipulation → sample → detection). DAG analysis verifies no circular causality.
use_cases: Identify topological ordering for forward simulation
dag.expected_result: Should be a DAG (no cycles) unless explicit feedback mechanisms exist (e.g., sample heating → temperature control → sample)

gap_detection.reason: CORE SCIENTIFIC DISCOVERY TOOL - Identify knowledge gaps (System D nodes with unknown properties)
use_cases: Identify 'orphaned' nodes (System D with no incoming measured edges)
Detect under-constrained systems (insufficient measurements to infer System D)
Find missing interactions that would enable gap closure

matrix_transformation.reason: ENABLES SVD GAP CLOSURE - Convert DAG to matrices for mathematical inference
use_cases: Generate adjacency matrix A (who connects to whom)
Solve for unknown properties: B = C × A⁻¹ (matrix gap closure)

centrality.reason: Identify critical components (System D - sample - should have high betweenness centrality)
use_cases: Verify sample is the 'bottleneck' between source and detection (high betweenness)
Prioritize measurements for gap closure (high centrality nodes)

paths.reason: Trace signal paths from source to detector

connectivity.reason: Ensure system is fully connected (no isolated components)
use_cases: Verify all components are reachable from source
Ensure sample is observable by at least one detector

reachability.reason: Verify System D (sample) is reachable from System A (source) and reaches System E (detection)
use_cases: Ensure sample is illuminated by source (via System B)

flow.reason: Model photon flux, particle flux, or signal strength propagation

cycles.reason: Identify feedback loops (e.g., sample heating → temperature change → sample properties)
use_cases: Distinguish physical feedback from measurement artifacts

gap_closure_workflow.description: Step-by-step workflow for using Reflow tools to infer System D (knowledge gap)

steps.name: Model experimental system as graph
steps.action: Define Systems A, B, C, D (as UNKNOWN), E with interactions

steps.name: Generate system-of-systems graph and detect gaps
steps.action: Verify System D is identified as a knowledge gap

steps.name: Transform DAG to matrices
steps.output: Adjacency matrix A, Measurement matrix B, Causal matrix C

steps.name: Apply SVD-based gap closure
steps.action: Analyze SVD singular values, infer System D constraints

steps.name: Validate gap closure proposals
steps.tool: Manual (scientist reviews proposals for physical plausibility)
steps.action: Generate testable predictions, design follow-up experiments

system_d.gap_closure_goal: Infer crystal structure and lattice parameters from diffraction pattern

beamline_example.gap_closure_strategy: Use measured diffraction pattern (sample → detector) combined with known source/optics (A, B) and environment (C) to infer crystal structure (D) via Bragg's law and structure factor analysis. SVD gap closure identifies missing d-spacings and systematic absences that constrain space group.

system_of_systems_graph_v2.py.generates: Experimental system graph, gap detection report, NetworkX analyses (DAG, centrality, paths)

reflow_gap_closure.py.generates: Gap closure proposals (inferred System D properties), matrix analysis, SVD results

matrix_gap_detection.py.function: Transforms DAG to matrices, applies SVD, solves B = C × A⁻¹ for unknowns

link_architectures.py.usage: Links functional architecture (WHAT we want to know) to experimental architecture (HOW we measure it)
link_architectures.py.function: Bridges scientific questions to experimental design

key_differences_from_standard_reflow.focus: Scientific discovery (inferring unknowns) vs. Engineering (building systems)
key_differences_from_standard_reflow.knowledge_gaps: EXPECTED and DESIRED (System D is the goal) vs. ERRORS to fix
key_differences_from_standard_reflow.validation: Physical plausibility and experimental testability vs. Functional correctness
key_differences_from_standard_reflow.workflow: Model → Detect gaps → Infer unknowns → Validate experimentally vs. Design → Implement → Test
key_differences_from_standard_reflow.success_metric: Quality of scientific hypotheses generated vs. System implementation completeness
